chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I enter with these people in the Maghrib prayer, and they hurry me so that I do not have time to call the Adhan and Iqamah, so I do not recite anything. Then when they bow, and I bow with them, will that suffice for me?' He said, 'Yes.'

This does not contradict what we have previously stated, because his saying 'so I did not recite anything' implies that he meant what was added to the Al-Hamd (Surah Al-Fatihah), since we have clarified that relying solely on Al-Hamd is sufficient in a state of necessity. And this report is not explicit in that he did not recite anything from Al-Hamd or other than it; rather, it is general (mujmal), while the first report is detailed (mufassal), and taking the detailed one is preferable to the general one, in addition to the fact that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, the narrator of this hadith, narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) without an intermediary, what we mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I join the prayer late and miss the Imam's recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for a latecomer (*muqtadi*) who joins the Maghrib prayer in ruku' and misses the Imam's recitation. The commentary by Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction by interpreting 'not reciting anything' as referring to the optional surah (*surah zaydah*) rather than the obligatory *Al-Fatihah*, which remains sufficient in cases of necessity (*darurah*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing detailed reports (*mufassal*) over general ones (*mujmal*) when determining ritual validity.
